name: SoftBank Group Corp.
monetization: Investment holding company whose AI monetization is portfolio appreciation: ~13% of OpenAI (planned), ~90% of Arm, ~40% of Stargate, Ampere — increasingly funded by asset sales and debt secured against those same stakes.
description_md: SoftBank Group is a Japanese investment holding company (Vision Funds, ~90%-owned Arm, and direct strategic stakes) that has repositioned itself as the single largest financial backer of OpenAI and co-lead of the Stargate buildout. Chairman-CEO Masayoshi Son has explicitly reoriented the balance sheet around artificial super-intelligence, selling legacy positions — the entire Nvidia stake ($5.83B, Oct 2025) and part of T-Mobile ($9.17B) — to fund the bet.
ai_monetization_md: SoftBank's AI exposure is equity-mark-driven, not operating revenue: $32.4B invested in OpenAI by March 2026 and planned to reach $64.6B (~13% of OpenAI) by October 1, 2026; ~90% of Arm (royalty and licensing leverage on AI silicon); Ampere Computing acquired for $6.5B (closed Nov 25, 2025) to build an Arm-based server-CPU stack; and ~40% of Stargate LLC, where SoftBank carries financial responsibility and Son serves as chairman. The thesis is concentrated, levered exposure to OpenAI's equity value and to the compute infrastructure it consumes.
risk_notes_md: The funding stack is increasingly debt against the AI portfolio itself: a bridge loan of up to $40B for the OpenAI investment (reported repayment deadline March 2027) and a $10B two-year margin loan collateralized by the OpenAI stake, signed August 2026 with Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Mizuho, Apollo Global Funding, and SMBC — with provisions requiring additional collateral or early repayment if OpenAI's preferred-share valuation falls sharply. OpenAI shares are unlisted, so collateral value rests on private-round marks rather than a traded price. Selling the Nvidia stake to fund OpenAI concentrated the balance sheet in a single private counterparty.

events.why_it_matters: SoftBank exited 32.1M NVDA shares (sold in October) — the clearest signal that its AI strategy is a concentrated OpenAI position funded by liquidating everything else.
